stem: A 16-year-old girl who helps run her household is being evaluated for TB preventive treatment after her father was diagnosed with MDR-TB two months ago. TBI testing (TST or IGRA) is not readily available at her clinic this month due to a supply shortage. Active TB disease has been ruled out in her through symptom screening and chest imaging. No HIV risk factors. Exam: well-appearing, no acute findings.

patient.social_history: Lives with parents; father diagnosed with MDR-TB two months ago
patient.presenting_complaint: Household contact evaluation for TB preventive treatment; TBI testing currently unavailable due to a local supply shortage
patient.prior_treatment: None; no prior TB treatment ever

distractors: The unavailability of TBI testing treated as a reason to defer any preventive treatment decision indefinitely rather than proceeding without it
Her age (16, not a young child) used as a reason to consider her lower priority for preventive treatment despite her documented household exposure
Her role managing the household used to argue she is otherwise healthy and therefore lower priority for preventive treatment
ntep_correct_actions: Offer this contact TB preventive treatment as standard practice regardless of her age; TPT must not be deferred because TBI testing is unavailable this month.

Recognize that identifying and following up household contacts like her is part of NTEP's standing, unconditional case-finding and contact-management activity, not contingent on a locally demonstrated prevalence threshold.
who_correct_actions: Treat TB preventive treatment for this contact (aged 5 years and older) as conditionally appropriate rather than standard practice; confirmation of TB infection with either IGRA or a skin test would be desirable before treating, given her age.

Treat this kind of contact-management activity as conditionally appropriate only where the local TB prevalence has been shown to meet the recommended threshold (approximately 0.5% or higher), rather than as a routine activity applied irrespective of a demonstrated local prevalence.
us_correct_actions: Treat this contact's TB preventive treatment as contingent on a confirmed positive TBI test, since this framework's regimens are framed around treatment of confirmed latent TB infection rather than an empiric approach when testing is unavailable.

Attribute the identification and follow-up of this contact to contact investigation following a known index case, consistent with this framework's passive, contact-investigation-driven model, rather than to population-level active case-finding policy.
critical_error_conditions: Concluding that no preventive treatment can be offered to this documented household contact simply because TBI testing is temporarily unavailable
expected_divergence_points: Whether TB preventive treatment for a household contact aged 5+ is standard, undeferred practice or a conditional recommendation where testing is desirable first
Whether this contact-management activity reflects standing, unconditional national program policy or is only appropriate where a threshold local prevalence is demonstrated
